guide.title: Fluid Resuscitation
guide.lead: Fluid is a drug: the right type, the right dose, the right patient. Bleeding patients need just enough to keep a radial pulse. Head injury and sepsis need more. Failing hearts need very little. Reassess after every bolus.

sections.title: Who gets what
rows: Boluses of about 250 mL to a radial pulse or systolic 80–90 mmHg; blood where available
Avoid hypotension: systolic at least 110 mmHg in most adults
At least 30 mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours
No large boluses; small challenge (250 mL) only if lungs clear

sections.title: Practical points
items: Isotonic crystalloid: 0.9% saline or a balanced solution (lactated Ringer's)
Large volumes of saline cause hyperchloremic acidosis
Dose = mL/kg × weight: 20 mL/kg × 70 kg = 1400 mL
IO access when IV fails in a critical patient

quiz.q: A 70 kg adult needs 20 mL/kg. Volume?
A risk of large volumes of 0.9% saline:
quiz.explanation: Balanced solutions such as lactated Ringer's avoid most of it.

quiz.q: Cardiogenic shock after anterior MI: BP 86/58, crackles halfway up, SpO₂ 88%. Fluid strategy?
options: No large bolus; a small cautious challenge only on medical direction, then PCI
quiz.explanation: With wet lungs, fluid worsens oxygenation.

quiz.q: Permissive hypotension target in bleeding without head injury:
quiz.explanation: Enough to perfuse, not enough to blow off clots.

quiz.q: Bleeding with a serious head injury. BP target?
options: Avoid hypotension: systolic at least 110 mmHg
quiz.explanation: Hypotension doubles the damage to an injured brain.

options: At least 30 mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours
quiz.explanation: Reassess for overload as you go.

quiz.q: Fluid bolus for a child in shock:
IV access fails in a peri-arrest patient. Next?
quiz.explanation: IO works for fluids and drugs.

quiz.q: A sign that the patient is responding to fluid:
options: Heart rate falling and mental status improving
quiz.explanation: Crackles and rising JVP mean overload.

options: Cold fluid worsens hypothermia and clotting

flashcards.question: Standard bolus
flashcards.answer: 20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid in many protocols; reassess after each. Bleeding: smaller boluses (about 250 mL).

flashcards.question: Saline vs lactated Ringer's
flashcards.answer: Both isotonic. Large volumes of saline cause hyperchloremic acidosis; balanced solutions are closer to plasma.

flashcards.question: Signs fluids are working
flashcards.answer: Clearer mental status, falling heart rate, rising BP, stronger pulses, warmer skin.

flashcards.question: Signs of fluid overload
flashcards.answer: New crackles, worse breathing, rising JVP: stop.

flashcards.question: IO access
flashcards.answer: Vascular access through the bone marrow when IV fails in a critical patient (arrest, shock, children).

flashcards.question: Large boluses in cardiogenic shock?
flashcards.answer: No: the failing heart can't move the volume, so it backs up into the lungs.

flashcards.question: MAST/PASG
flashcards.answer: No longer used: no survival benefit.

flashcards.question: Septic shock fluids
flashcards.answer: At least 30 mL/kg crystalloid within the first 3 hours, reassessing for overload.

critical.scenario: An 80 kg man was stabbed in the abdomen. A pressure dressing slows the bleeding. HR 116, BP 98/72, anxious. Trauma centre 15 minutes away.
critical.question: Fluid strategy?

options.t: IV access en route; small boluses (about 250 mL) only if the radial pulse weakens or systolic falls below 80–90 mmHg

options.f: Normalising BP can wash out clots.
Get access en route in case he deteriorates.

options.t: Stay on scene until BP is normal

critical.explanation: The definitive fix is surgical bleeding control; don't delay transport for fluids.
critical.kpi: Applies permissive hypotension with appropriate crystalloid dosing in penetrating trauma

critical.scenario: A 65-year-old with heart failure and COPD: crackles everywhere, raised JVP, pink frothy sputum. BP 110/70, HR 104, SpO₂ 84%. A student suggests a 20 mL/kg bolus.
critical.question: Correct fluid plan?

options.t: No fluid: this is cardiogenic pulmonary edema. CPAP, nitrates per protocol, upright, transport

options.f: That could tip him into respiratory failure.

options.t: Lie him flat and give fluid

critical.explanation: IV access is for drugs here, not volume.
critical.kpi: Identifies cardiogenic pulmonary oedema and appropriately withholds fluids

critical.scenario: A 4-year-old (16 kg) with 2 days of vomiting and diarrhea is drowsy, with cold hands, capillary refill 4 seconds and HR 170. Lungs clear.
critical.question: Fluid plan?

options.t: IV or IO access; 10–20 mL/kg bolus, reassess after each

options.f: A drowsy child in shock needs IV or IO fluid.

critical.explanation: 16 kg × 20 mL/kg = 320 mL; stop for crackles, a big liver or worse breathing.
critical.kpi: Doses pediatric fluid boluses by weight and reassesses
